title: Closed-pair rigidity for supported three-term scalar local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, without a common annihilator, the actual restriction $H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ is bijective for every $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Choose a finite chain
$$S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}T_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0'=T,$$
where each arrow is either a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $J_k=(a_k)_!$ in the open case and $J_k=(a_k)_*$ in the closed case, and put $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r$, with $J=\mathrm{id}$ for $r=0$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. The symbol $T_0'$ is only the root of this chain; the closed member of the pair is $T_0$.
Let $L^{-1}\xrightarrow{b}L^0\xrightarrow{c}L^1$ be module sheaves on $S$ with $cb=0$. Each term $L^a$ has a finite constant scalar local model [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there are a pro-étale cover $\{U_i\to S\}$ and finitely presented scalar $\Lambda(*)$-modules $P_i$, which may depend on $i$, with $L^a|_{U_i}\cong\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P_i$, the scalar ring and the modules $P_i$ interpreted as constant sheaves on $U_i$. Covers and scalar modules may differ for the three terms. The maps $b,c$ are arbitrary actual module maps. Put $N=\ker c/\operatorname{im}b$. Then the actual derived restriction is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$,
$$R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},J(N)[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},t^*J(N)[0]).$$
It is natural in morphisms of the three-term complexes and uses the exact module inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient identification. No constructibility or completeness is required of $N$. Neither $b,c$ nor their pullbacks are required to be constant scalar matrices. No properness, henselian base, Noetherianity, or invertibility of $\ell$ is assumed. In particular the complement of the original $t$ need not be quasi-compact; the quasi-compact complement requirement applies only to the chain arrows. Empty schemes, zero modules, the zero coefficient ring, and $r=0$ are included.

proof.text: Exact J carries either row to a short exact row. The single-complex functor preserves finite limits and colimits, so Mathlib triangleOfSES gives a distinguished triangle of the resulting degree-zero complexes. closed_restriction_derived_operations gives triangulated source and target section functors and shift compatibility of the actual restriction. Its naturality gives the first two squares of a morphism of triangles; the shift compatibility gives the connecting-arrow square. Its components are the actual restriction components.

The image node that was equivalent to the item is gone. The finite-model comparison B_Λ(t) is now proved separately. Steps 2-3 prove the finite discrete case: lem-pe-finite-discrete-scalar-constant-models and det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist show the model is classical; constructible strata come from the qc chain complements on qcqs T, so det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical and sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves apply; then sk-prop-sf-comparison, comparison-pullback and the underlying-module comparison (which commutes with restriction) carry over the torsion hypothesis. Step 4 uses the new integral Rlim-tower node; its F_n are killed by ℓ^k, so each ρ_n is invertible and Rlim of the towers stays an isomorphism. Step 5 uses the new conditional rational transfer and the new Ω transfer, which keeps the full C(P,Ω) ring. Step 7 applies the new conditional image node, with B_Λ as an explicit premise, to b and c. Steps 1, 6 and 8-11 are the formal argument checked in the previous review: J and t^* are exact, the two short exact rows, the exact-source horseshoe morphism of triangles, and two-out-of-three in the right order. lean.statement: theorem supported_three_term_scalar_rigidity (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hΛ : (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : DiscreteTopology A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A), Finite A ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a : A, (ℓ ^ n) • a = 0) ∧ Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj A))) ∨ Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ])) ∨ (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ, Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E))) ∨ Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℚ_[ℓ])) ∨ (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ, Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E)))) {T₀ T S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T] [CompactSpace T₀] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T₀] (t : T₀ ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion t] (ht : ∀ (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}), Scheme.IsTorsionAbelianSheaf F → ∀ q : ℕ, Function.Bijective (Etale.cohomologyMap t F q)) (tree : QcqsOpenClosedTree T) (p : tree.Path S) (L : ShortComplex (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ S))) (hL₁ : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S L.X₁) (hL₂ : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S L.X₂) (hL₃ : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S L.X₃) : IsIso ((Functor.rightDerivedPullback (upperStar Λ t) ((Functor.whiskerRight (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction Λ t).unit (condensedModuleSections Λ T) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (upperStar Λ t) (Functor.whiskerLeft (Mod.forget (condensedRingObj Λ T₀)) ((sheafSections (Scheme.ProEt.topology T₀) Ab.{u + 1}).map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk (pullback.lift t (𝟙 T₀) ((Category.comp_id t).trans (Category.id_comp t).symm)) (pullback.lift_snd _ _ _)).op))) : condensedModuleSections Λ T ⟶ upperStar Λ t ⋙ condensedModuleSections Λ T₀)).app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj ((p.extension Λ).obj L.homology)))
lean.note: Support chains are represented by arbitrary paths (not necessarily leaf paths) in the existing QcqsOpenClosedTree. Every chain in the statement is such a path after adjoining complementary siblings as leaves; no rigidity is assumed on these siblings. The restriction is written directly as rightDerivedPullback of the actual section map. This is definitionally the body of torsionRigidityDerivedRestriction, avoiding an import of the downstream Serre-transfer theorem and any dependency cycle. The six original coefficient cases are explicit because the current general admissibility predicate also has a distinct finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure case.
